sentences.text: As per the DAR, the petitioner is a resident of Bindapur, Delhi.

On 31.05.2019, the petitioner,
along with her husband, went to visit the sister of her husband at her house in Tara Nagar, Kakrola.
After attending the meeting, the petitioner was returning home along with her husband.
At about 9:20 p.m., they were crossing the road from Tara Nagar towards MCD School, with the petitioner following her husband.

At that time, a motorcycle bearing registration no. DL 9S BS 0565, carrying two boys and being driven in a rash and negligent manner, came from the side of Old Palam Road Chowk and hit the petitioner.
As a result of the impact, the petitioner fell on the road and the motorcyclist also fell along with the motorcycle.
Her husband attempted to apprehend the driver of the motorcycle, but he fled from the spot.
Thereafter, her husband informed the police, and the petitioner was taken to Tarak Hospital by her son.

2.1 During the course of investigation, upon obtaining medical opinion on MLC no. 544/19 dated 31.05.2019, the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident were opined to be grievous in nature.
Further, respondent no. 1 failed to produce a driving licence valid on the date of the accident.
Accordingly, the offence initially registered under Sections 279/337 IPC was converted into one under Sections 279/338 IPC and Sections 3/181 of the MV Act.

The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary damages (Special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalisation, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:

(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
